title: Set Up Apple Mail for macOS
cardText: Set up iCloud, Google, Microsoft Exchange, IMAP and POP accounts in Apple Mail.
Configure email servers, authentication, SMTP and POP message retention.
Synchronise server mail or safely migrate local On My Mac mailboxes and MBOX archives without duplicates.
text: This guide covers Apple Mail on macOS.
Use Mail's automatic account setup or the provider's documented manual settings.
IMAP, iCloud Mail and Exchange normally synchronise server-stored messages and mailboxes.
Check On My Mac mailboxes, old POP messages and local archives before retiring the original Mac.
Use Mailbox, Export Mailbox to preserve local mailboxes as MBOX packages.
Use File, Import Mailboxes for supported Apple Mail and MBOX imports.
Apple Mail places imported mail in a separate Import mailbox for review.
Compare imported messages with the current mailbox before copying only missing messages.
Verify server synchronisation and keep the original backup until migration is complete.

identifySetupType.title: Identify the email setup or migration
body: Determine whether this is a new email account or an existing mailbox being moved to another Mac.
Identify the original email application and account type.
IMAP, iCloud Mail and Exchange normally restore server-stored messages.
POP mail and On My Mac mailboxes may exist only on the original computer.
If required local mail exists, protect it before changing accounts or replacing the computer.

identifyExistingClient.title: Identify the original email application
body: Determine whether the existing mail is in Apple Mail, Outlook, Thunderbird or another email client.
Identify whether its account uses IMAP, Exchange or POP.
Check the original client for local-only folders and separate archives.
If the original application is Apple Mail, locate its On My Mac mailboxes.
If the original client is different, identify the supported mail export format.
Do not delete the old account or remove the original installation before protecting local data.

checkExistingAppleMail.title: Check existing Apple Mail data
body: Open Mail on the original Mac.
Choose Mail, Settings, Accounts and identify the email account type.
Inspect Inbox, Sent, Archive and custom mailboxes.
Expand On My Mac in the Mail sidebar and check for locally stored messages.
Compare server-backed folders with webmail where available.
Identify any local POP messages or archives that do not exist on the server.
Check whether Time Machine or another backup system protects the original Mail data.
Do not remove the account while required local messages remain unprotected.

backupAppleMail.title: Back up local Apple Mail messages
body: On the original Mac, identify required On My Mac mailboxes and locally stored POP messages.
Select the required mailbox in the Mail sidebar.
Choose Mailbox, Export Mailbox.
Select an external drive or another reliable backup location.
Repeat for each required local mailbox or select multiple mailboxes where appropriate.
Mail exports mailboxes as .mbox packages.
Keep the original folder names and record which mailboxes were exported.
Check that exported packages exist and contain the expected data.
For a complete Mac migration, also consider a verified Time Machine or supported Migration Assistant backup.
Keep an untouched backup of the original data.

link.description: Official Apple Mail mailbox export instructions.

link.name: Apple: Restore Files with Time Machine
link.description: Official Time Machine recovery and restoration instructions.

backupOtherClientMail.title: Back up mail from another application
body: Identify the previous email application's storage format.
For Thunderbird, export required local mailboxes in a compatible MBOX format.
For Outlook, preserve PST files and check whether a supported conversion or transfer method is required.
Do not rename a PST file to MBOX; changing the extension does not convert the messages.
Check whether the required messages already exist in the destination server mailbox.
Preserve locally stored Sent mail, archives and custom folders.
Keep an untouched source backup before attempting import.

link.name: Apple: Import Mailboxes into Mail
link.description: Official supported Apple Mail and MBOX import formats.

protectOriginalMail.title: Protect the original email data
body: The required local messages or mailboxes have not been backed up.
Preserve the original Mac, email application and local mail data.
Check On My Mac, old POP folders, Sent mail and archives.
Create and verify an export or reliable computer backup.
Do not delete accounts or overwrite the source Mail data.
Resume migration only after the original data is protected.

identifyAccountType.title: Identify the email provider and protocol
body: Determine whether the provider is iCloud, Google, Microsoft Exchange, Microsoft 365 or another hosting service.
Use the provider's supported account type wherever possible.
For third-party hosted mail, confirm whether IMAP or POP is required.
IMAP is generally preferred when messages and folders must synchronise across devices.
POP primarily downloads incoming mail and may leave important historical messages stored locally.
Check the provider's current authentication and connection requirements.

link.name: Apple: Add an Email Account
link.description: Official Apple Mail account setup instructions.

collectProviderSettings.title: Collect manual mail server settings
body: Obtain the email address and the username required by the hosting provider.
Confirm whether the incoming server uses IMAP or POP.
Record the incoming server hostname, port and encryption method.
Record the outgoing SMTP hostname, port and authentication requirements.
Common IMAP settings use port 993 with SSL/TLS.
Common POP settings use port 995 with SSL/TLS.
Common SMTP submission ports include 587 with STARTTLS and 465 with implicit TLS.
Confirm these values against the provider's documentation.
Check whether OAuth, multifactor authentication or an app-specific password is required.

link.name: Apple: Change Mail Server Settings
link.description: Official incoming and outgoing server configuration options.

obtainProviderSettings.title: Obtain the correct provider configuration
body: The required incoming or outgoing server settings are unavailable.
Check the email provider's current Apple Mail configuration instructions.
Confirm the protocol, server names, ports, encryption and authentication.
Do not guess server hostnames or disable encryption to force a connection.
Continue after confirming the correct settings.

addEmailAccount.title: Add the email account in Apple Mail
body: Open Mail on the Mac.
Choose Mail, Add Account.
Enter the email address or select the relevant account provider from the available list.
Select Continue and follow the account setup prompts.
For iCloud, Google or Microsoft Exchange, use the provider's supported sign-in process.
Complete any multifactor authentication or browser approval.
For Other Mail Account, enter the required account details and allow Mail to attempt configuration.
If automatic detection fails, check the provider's documented manual settings.
Complete setup and confirm the account appears in the Mail sidebar.

link.name: Apple: Add and Manage Mail Accounts
link.description: Official instructions for adding email accounts on macOS.

addEmailAccount.alt: Apple Mail account setup dialog showing supported email providers
addEmailAccount.caption: Choose the email provider or Other Mail Account, then complete the account sign-in process.

troubleshootAccountSetup.title: Investigate account setup problems
body: Record the exact error displayed by Apple Mail.
Confirm the Mac has a working internet connection.
Check the correct email address, account type and provider settings.
Review Mail, Settings, Accounts, Server Settings.
Check incoming and outgoing server authentication.
Confirm whether the provider requires a browser sign-in, OAuth or an app-specific password.
Check for a provider outage or account restriction.
Do not disable encryption or switch to POP simply because IMAP setup failed.
Correct the identified issue before testing again.

link.name: Apple: Mail Cannot Send or Receive
link.description: Official troubleshooting for macOS Mail connections.

link.name: Apple: Change Server Settings
link.description: Official server configuration instructions.

testEmailConnection.title: Test sending and receiving
body: Confirm that the account appears in the Mail sidebar.
Send a test email to another accessible address.
Reply from that address and verify the reply arrives.
Check that the sent message appears in the expected Sent mailbox.
Check for offline account indicators, Outbox errors or authentication prompts.
For a POP account, confirm the message download and local storage behaviour.
Once sending and receiving work, identify the configured account type before assessing old mail.

checkAccountSyncType.title: Does the mailbox synchronise from the server?
body: Open Mail, Settings, Accounts and identify the configured account type.
IMAP, iCloud Mail and Exchange normally synchronise server-stored messages and folders.
POP mail may contain messages that were downloaded only to the original Mac.
For IMAP or Exchange, verify normal server synchronisation before importing an archive.
For POP, determine whether historical local messages must be transferred.

verifyServerSyncedMail.title: Verify synchronised mailboxes
body: Allow Apple Mail time to synchronise the server mailbox.
Compare Inbox, Sent, Drafts, Archive and custom folders with webmail where available.
Check a selection of older messages and attachments.
Expand mailbox groups in the Mail sidebar to reveal available folders.
Check whether mailbox filtering or account connection problems are hiding expected messages.
If a message exists in webmail but not in Mail, investigate synchronisation rather than importing old mail.
If the required server mail is present, continue to the local-only mailbox check.

investigateSyncMissing.title: Determine where missing messages are stored
body: Search the provider's webmail for the missing messages.
Check Archive, Trash and other server folders.
If the messages exist in webmail, look for a connection, filter or mailbox display problem in Mail.
If the messages are absent from webmail but present on the old Mac, they may be stored under On My Mac or in an old POP mailbox.
Do not import the complete old mailbox before determining where the missing messages are located.

troubleshootMailSync.title: Resolve Apple Mail synchronisation problems
body: Check whether the correct mail account is enabled and online.
Review mailbox filters, search scope and folder visibility.
Check Mail, Settings, Accounts and the account's Server Settings.
If messages appear missing or the mailbox index is inconsistent, review Apple's Mailbox, Rebuild option.
For IMAP, rebuilding may cause locally cached messages to be downloaded again.
Do not rebuild a POP or local mailbox without first protecting its local data.
Allow synchronisation to complete, then compare with webmail again.

link.name: Apple: Create and Rebuild Mailboxes
link.description: Official mailbox management and Rebuild instructions.

link.name: Apple: Mail Connection Troubleshooting
link.description: Official help for missing or unavailable messages.

checkMissingMailSource.title: Check for local-only missing messages
body: Inspect the original Mac and email application.
Check On My Mac, old POP mailboxes, local Sent messages and exported archives.
Search other user accounts or relevant email applications where appropriate.
If required messages exist locally but not in webmail, protect them before transferring.
If the messages cannot be found locally or on the server, investigate available backups.
Do not import unrelated message archives as a substitute for locating the missing data.

checkLocalOnlyData.title: Check for On My Mac and other local-only data
body: Inspect the original Apple Mail installation after verifying server synchronisation.
Expand On My Mac and check for stored mailboxes and historical messages.
Check old POP Inbox, Sent, Archive and custom folders.
Check for separate MBOX exports or messages saved locally.
Mailboxes under On My Mac do not automatically synchronise to an IMAP or Exchange server.
Check local contacts, calendars, rules and signatures separately where required.
If all required email exists on the server and no local mail is missing, no import is required.
If required local messages exist, verify a backup before migration.

link.name: Apple: On My Mac and Server Mailboxes
link.description: Explains local versus synchronised mailbox storage.

checkPopMigration.title: Check whether previous POP mail is needed
body: Determine whether the POP account is newly configured or replacing an existing installation.
Inspect the original Mac for downloaded POP messages and local Sent mail.
Compare the original Inbox, Sent and custom folders with the new Mail installation.
POP will not restore messages previously deleted from the server.
If all required historical messages are already available, no import is needed.
If local-only POP mail must be transferred, preserve an export or verified backup first.

confirmLocalBackup.title: Confirm the original local mail backup
body: Locate the required On My Mac, POP or exported mailbox data.
For Apple Mail, use Mailbox, Export Mailbox for supported local mailbox exports.
Preserve .mbox packages and their original folder identification.
If the source is another application, use its supported export or conversion method.
Verify that the backup includes the necessary Inbox, Sent and custom folders.
Keep an untouched source copy separate from the migration working files.
Do not begin an import until the original local data has been protected.

link.name: Apple: Import and Export Mailboxes
link.description: Official Apple Mail mailbox export procedure.

identifyMailSource.title: Identify the old mail source
body: Check whether the required mail is in Apple Mail MBOX packages, another application's MBOX files or another archive format.
Apple Mail supports importing mailboxes exported from Mail and compatible MBOX sources.
Some Outlook PST archives require a compatible conversion or intermediary email client.
Do not rename a PST or another unsupported format to .mbox.
Decide whether local-only messages must remain a separate archive or appear in a synchronised mailbox.
Use a method that does not overwrite the current Mail account or existing messages.

checkOtherFormat.title: Prepare another email archive format
body: Identify the source application and actual archive format.
If an Outlook PST is involved, use Outlook or a compatible migration tool to export or transfer the required messages.
If messages are available through an IMAP account, consider transferring only missing messages using the original supported client.
For EML or other exported messages, check whether the source can produce a compatible MBOX mailbox.
Avoid unverified conversion utilities and preserve the original data.
Continue only after a supported import source is available.

prepareImport.title: Prepare a safe Apple Mail import
body: Keep an untouched backup of the original mailbox exports.
Check available Mac disk space for the imported messages.
Compare the source archive with the destination mailbox to identify possible overlap.
Do not import source messages directly into existing Inbox or Sent folders.
Apple Mail normally creates a separate Import mailbox when using File, Import Mailboxes.
Keep the original mailbox structure identifiable.
Check the destination server's storage quota if imported messages will later be uploaded to IMAP.
Do not repeat imports until the earlier import result has been reviewed.

importMailboxes.title: Import Apple Mail or MBOX mailboxes
body: Open Apple Mail on the destination Mac.
Choose File, Import Mailboxes.
For mailboxes exported from Apple Mail or an appropriate previous Mail data folder, select Apple Mail.
For supported MBOX archives from other sources, choose Files in mbox format.
Select the source folder or mailbox package and continue.
Follow the import instructions and allow the operation to finish.
Apple Mail creates an Import mailbox in the sidebar for imported messages.
Expand Import and inspect its subfolders.
Do not move the entire Import mailbox directly into a populated account folder.
Keep the original source archive until the imported messages have been verified.

link.name: Apple: Import or Export Mailboxes
link.description: Official Mail import instructions and Import mailbox behaviour.

importMailboxes.alt: Apple Mail File menu displaying the Import Mailboxes command
importMailboxes.caption: Choose File, Import Mailboxes and select the supported Apple Mail or MBOX source.

checkPartialImport.title: Investigate an incomplete import
body: Do not immediately repeat the entire import.
Inspect the Import mailbox and identify which folders and messages were transferred.
Compare message dates, counts and attachments with the source.
Check for insufficient disk space, unsupported source formats and damaged archive files.
Correct the identified problem before retrying.
If another import is required, keep it separately identifiable to avoid confusing repeated copies.
Preserve the original archive and any partially imported mail.

reviewImportedMail.title: Review imported messages for duplicates
body: Open the Import mailbox and its subfolders.
Compare the imported messages with the existing Inbox, Sent, Archive and custom folders.
Look for duplicate messages using sender, recipient, subject, date, contents and attachments.
Messages sharing the same subject are not necessarily duplicates.
Confirm that important older POP messages and local Sent mail are present.
Avoid deleting messages based only on matching subjects or dates.
For large mailboxes, review smaller batches.
Keep uncertain messages isolated in Import instead of merging them.

resolveImportDuplicates.title: Resolve duplicate or missing imported messages
body: Compare suspected duplicates with messages already in the destination mailbox.
Check message contents and attachments before deciding that two messages are identical.
Delete confirmed redundant staging copies only after verifying the required message exists elsewhere.
If messages are missing, inspect other source mailboxes and exported packages.
Avoid repeating a complete import without understanding the previous result.
Keep the original mailbox exports unchanged.
If the imported data cannot be reconciled safely, retain it as a separate archive.

chooseMailDestination.title: Keep imported mail local or upload to the server
body: Decide whether the imported messages should remain in a separate On My Mac archive.
An On My Mac mailbox is local and does not synchronise across devices.
For historical access on one Mac, a separate local archive may be sufficient.
If the old messages must appear on other devices, they need to be copied into an appropriate server mailbox.
Do not merge all imported messages into existing folders without checking for duplicates.
Preserve the source archive and any retained local staging copies.

prepareServerStaging.title: Create a separate server staging mailbox
body: Confirm the destination IMAP or Exchange account is connected and synchronising.
In Mail, choose Mailbox, New Mailbox.
In the Location menu, choose the destination server account rather than On My Mac.
Create a mailbox named Imported Old Mail.
Mailboxes created under an account are intended to be stored on that account's server.
Check server storage quotas before uploading large archives.
Do not copy directly into a populated Inbox or Sent mailbox.
Keep the original Import mailbox unchanged during the initial transfer.

link.name: Apple: Create Mailboxes in Mail
link.description: Official instructions for local and server mailbox locations.

copyMailToServer.title: Copy reviewed messages to the server
body: Select the reviewed messages in the Import mailbox.
Control-click the selection and choose Copy To, then the server's Imported Old Mail mailbox.
Alternatively, hold Option while dragging the selected messages to the destination mailbox.
Work in manageable batches and preserve useful subfolder organisation.
Allow Mail time to upload the messages.
Check webmail to verify that the copied messages appear on the server.
Do not delete the local Import mailbox or source backup until the server copies have been verified.
Do not repeat an interrupted batch before checking which messages arrived.

link.name: Apple: Move or Copy Emails
link.description: Official Copy To and Option-drag instructions.

checkPartialUpload.title: Check an incomplete server transfer
body: Do not immediately repeat the entire transfer.
Compare the server's Imported Old Mail mailbox with the local Import mailbox.
Check webmail to identify which messages have already arrived.
Investigate mailbox quota limits, connection errors and oversized messages.
Correct the issue and copy only missing items where practical.
Use separately labelled batches if the upload result remains uncertain.
Preserve the local and original archive copies.

chooseMergeMethod.title: Keep the server archive separate or merge
body: Decide whether Imported Old Mail should remain a separate historical server mailbox.
Keeping it separate makes the old messages available across devices without changing existing Inbox or Sent mail.
If messages must appear in their original destination folders, compare them with existing messages first.
Copy only confirmed missing messages.
Do not assume Apple Mail automatically prevents every duplicate.
Keep staging copies and source backups until the final result is verified.

mergeReviewedMail.title: Merge only missing messages
body: Identify which messages in Imported Old Mail are absent from their intended destination folders.
Copy only the missing messages into the appropriate Inbox, Sent, Archive or custom mailbox.
Use Control-click, Copy To or Option-drag to preserve the staging source.
Transfer in manageable batches.
Allow server synchronisation to complete.
Verify the final messages and attachments in webmail.
Do not delete staging folders or original archive files until the merge is confirmed.

link.name: Apple: Copy Messages Between Mailboxes
link.description: Official instructions for copying selected messages.

verifyMigratedMail.title: Verify migrated mailboxes and messages
body: Compare the destination Mail installation with the original mailbox exports.
Check Inbox, Sent, Archive, Import, On My Mac and any important custom mailboxes.
Open older messages and verify attachments.
Check message dates, contents and mailbox organisation.
Look for duplicates after any merge.
For IMAP or Exchange, confirm that server-bound messages are visible in webmail.
For local-only archives, confirm the messages remain accessible on the Mac and are backed up.
Check contacts, calendars, rules and signatures separately where required.
Keep the original exports until migration has been verified.

migrationEscalation.title: Further Apple Mail migration required
body: The required messages could not be imported, uploaded or reconciled safely.
Preserve the original Mac and exported mailbox packages.
Keep incomplete imports separate from the current mailbox.
Record the original application, archive format, macOS version and any errors.
Check source compatibility, available disk space and server mailbox quotas.
For unsupported PST or other formats, investigate a supported export or conversion method.
Do not repeat full imports or merge uncertain messages.
Consider restoring required local data from a verified Time Machine backup.

link.name: Apple: Import and Export Mailboxes
link.description: Official import and export instructions.

link.name: Apple: Restore with Time Machine
link.description: Official backup restoration instructions.

setupComplete.title: Apple Mail setup completed
body: The email account is configured and can send and receive messages.
Incoming and outgoing server settings are correct.
For IMAP, iCloud Mail or Exchange, required server-stored messages and mailboxes have synchronised.
If there was no missing local-only data, no mailbox import was required.
For POP, required locally stored messages have been retained or transferred.
Any imported mail has been reviewed for duplicates before merging into existing mailboxes.
Check contacts, calendars, rules and signatures separately when required.
Keep verified backups of important local email data.

setupEscalation.title: Further Apple Mail account diagnostics
body: The email account cannot send or receive after checking the configured provider settings.
Record the macOS version, email provider, protocol and exact error message.
Confirm that the provider supports the selected account type and authentication method.
Check OAuth, multifactor authentication and security restrictions.
Compare account access through webmail.
Investigate connection status, mail server settings and mailbox storage limits.
Do not remove the original account until required local mail has been protected.

link.description: Official Apple Mail troubleshooting instructions.
